subject.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session

question: Is the current terminal/test evidence enough to merge this session-recovery PR, or should maintainers require direct after-fix proof of a same-session `reply session initialization conflicted` recovery before choosing between this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a mechanical code defect; it is proof sufficiency and canonical-branch selection for a high-impact session-state and message-delivery recovery path.

options.title: Require direct recovery proof
options.body: Ask for redacted logs, terminal output, recording, or linked artifact from this head showing the reported second same-session message recovering from the init conflict and receiving a real reply.

options.title: Choose the competing branch
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the canonical implementation only if maintainers prefer its shape and can obtain equivalent proof there.

options.title: Accept the current evidence
options.body: Merge this PR based on source review, forced-conflict tests, and urgency, while explicitly owning the session-state and delivery risk.

recommendation.title: Require direct recovery proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted logs, terminal output, recording, or linked artifact from this head showing the reported second same-session message recovering from the init conflict and receiving a real reply.

likelyOwner.reason: Their guarded reply-session initialization work is the closest recent ownership signal for the changed boundary.
